basis: Hypertrichosis and neuropathy define it; skeletal deformities reported in 3/4 cases and periostitis in 30-79%. Retinal anomalies lack documented functional damage.

decisions.ocular: none: retinal anomalies are reported in familial cases (3/4), but their nature and damaging effect are unspecified.

basis: Spastic paraplegia with distal amyotrophy and characteristic skeletal deformities defines this syndrome; constipation and dysphagia do not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: distal amyotrophy is a defining feature, including in the synonym; skeletal deformities are also characteristic (30-79%; several in 2/2).

basis: Methionine synthase deficiency with defining megaloblastic anemia and neurodevelopmental impairment/epilepsy; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish hepatic injury.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental impairment and epilepsy are core features in the definition of this metabolic-anemia-neurologic syndrome.

basis: Thoracic skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia is usual and cystic renal dysplasia is common (approximately >=30%). Hepatic, cardiac and CNS abnormalities are mostly <30%.

decisions.renal: involved: cystic renal dysplasia is a characteristic, common visceral lesion of severe Majewski/SRTD6 (approximately >=30%); HPO gives no exact frequency.

basis: Marfanoid skeletal habitus and advanced bone age define the syndrome; inguinal hernia reflects an abdominal-wall defect, without established intrinsic intestinal damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: an inguinal hernia alone establishes an abdominal-wall defect, not direct damage to bowel or another gastrointestinal organ.

basis: Destructive bone remodeling; hearing loss in 1/1 and premature tooth loss is characteristic (estimated >=30%). Neurologic compression frequency unclear; no primary endocrine/metabolic defect.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: premature tooth loss from resorptive dental involvement is characteristic of this early-onset RANK disorder (estimated >=30%; HPO unquantified).
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: abnormal bone remodeling is skeletal disease; the metabolic-bone ancestor and secondary hypercalcemia do not establish an independent metabolic/endocrine disorder.

basis: Immune dysregulation; destructive nephritis, vasculitis/MI and cerebral hemorrhage each in 1/1. Cholangitis omitted at cap; lung/joint damage unsupported by patient phenotypes.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: vasculitis and myocardial infarction directly damage vessels/heart in 1/1; the defining entity is systemic immune dysregulation.
decisions.renal: involved: glomerulonephritis, CKD, sclerosis, fibrosis and tubular atrophy demonstrate direct renal damage in 1/1; these are manifestations of immune dysregulation.

basis: Localized lipogranulomatous lesions arise in sinonasal tissue and subcutis; altered erythrocytes within lesions do not establish a systemic blood-cell disease.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: subcutaneous lipogranulomatous lesions are an established disease location, reflected by the synonym subcutaneous spherulocystic disease.

basis: Developmental disability defines syndrome; obesity 80-99%, skeletal deformities and progressive hearing loss 30-79%. Myopia/ptosis and dental anomalies omitted at cap.

decisions.ocular: none under cap: myopia/ptosis occur in 30-79%, but more frequent obesity and substantial skeletal/hearing abnormalities take priority.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: syndromic truncal obesity occurs in 80-99%; it is a direct metabolic phenotype, without requiring a separate endocrine-gland lesion.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: scoliosis, limb/joint and skeletal anomalies occur in 30-79%; these are associated structural manifestations of the neurodevelopmental syndrome.

basis: Functional disease of phagocytic blood cells causes immunodeficiency; abnormal counts are not required for the blood-cell axis. Other affected sites vary across subtypes.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this is a disease of phagocytic blood-cell function; the rule includes blood-cell diseases without requiring cytopenias, marrow failure or coagulopathy.
